title: Rate Policy Playground — wireframe journal and backlog notes
body:
Context / goal:
This doc captures a lightweight, rough-running set of ideas for a Rate Policy Playground: an interactive console page where operators and power users can simulate, debug, and tune rate limits / quota policies per-credential and per-route, with immediate feedback and exported guidance for engineers. Primary audience: product ops, SRE, platform teams, and advanced customers during Dedicated/Private onboarding.

What problem we solve:
- People can't easily reason about compounded rate rules (global + per-key + route overrides + burst windows).
- On-call and solutions-engineering spend time reproducing throttle incidents to craft policy fixes.
- Customers want to preview how a policy change will affect tail latency and 95th/99th error rates before rollout.

High-level interactions (wireframe sketches):
1) Top strip: Policy selector + active environment (prod / staging / dedicated pool) + date/traffic profile dropdown (default: last 7d, spike, sustained heavy).
2) Left column (playground controls):
   - Credential chooser (searchable) with quick toggles: "apply policy to sample key", clone-as-template, pin-to-view.
   - Route filter tags (chat, embeddings, rerank, custom routes).
   - Policy builder block: compose rules in order of precedence. Small inline examples: "global: 1000 r/s", "route: /chat -> 500 r/s", "key: ABC... -> 200 r/s, burst 1000 tokens/5m".
   - Temporal slider to set burst window + smoothing.
3) Middle: Live simulation canvas
   - Timeline with stacked lanes per route showing requests, throttles, and fallback events. Hover reveals payload size (tokens) and latency contribution.
   - Heatmap overlay for token-cost vs throttle probability.
   - Simulation controls: play / step / jump-to-incident timestamps.
4) Right: Insights + recommended fixes
   - Real-time metrics updated by simulation: expected qps, throttle rate (pct), latency p50/p95, estimated cost delta.
   - Automated suggestions: "reduce global by 10%" or "add route exception for /chat/stream" with confidence scores (low/med/high) and rationale.
   - Quick export: JSON policy diff, Terraform snippet, policy patch URL for rollout.

Sketch details and micro-UX notes:
- Credential chooser should show "last seen" and "top route usage" to reduce flip-flopping. Small pill with usage % of total.
- When composing rules, show visual precedence stack: topmost rule highlighted in timeline when it triggers.
- Allow users to annotate simulated incidents with notes that map back to tickets (copyable link).
- Provide a small "what-if" mode that only changes simulation, not deployment config. A separate "apply" CTA commits to staging/rollout.
- Keyboard shortcuts for iterating rule sets (cmd+enter = run sim, cmd+s = save as template).

Backlog / acceptance criteria (MVP slice):
- [P0] Playground page accessible from Console -> Traffic -> Rate playground.
- [P0] Load historical traffic profile (last 24h / last 7d) and replay at variable speed.
- [P0] Add/modify simple rules: global, per-key, per-route, burst window; simulation shows throttle pct and per-route tokens.
- [P1] Export policy diff as JSON and copy-to-clipboard.
- [P1] Small recommendation engine (heuristic) that flags obvious misconfigs (e.g., per-route higher than global).
- [P2] Integration with rollout system: create canary with policy patch.

Edge cases / open questions (to discuss with SRE & infra):
- How faithful must simulation be to runtime hystrix-style batching behavior and KV-caching? Initial MVP should approximate token accounting and queueing; exact batching behavior is tricky.
- Should we surface downstream fallback behavior (automatic model fallback) in simulation? Suggest toggle.
- Data retention: replay profiles will need sampled request traces. What's the retention policy and PII masking? Work with security team.

Metrics to validate utility:
- time-to-resolution for throttle incidents (goal: -30% for triaged incidents using playground).
- % of policy edits that require rollback after 24h.
- adoption: number of simulations run per team / week.

Design notes for visual language:
- Timeline lanes use low-saturation reds for throttles, teal for normal traffic, and pale amber for burst windows.
- Use token-heatmap color scale separate from throttle severity to avoid confusion.
- Tooltips include links to related console pages: per-credential usage, per-route latency graphs.

Implementation constraints / infra notes:
- Simulation should run client-side for small profiles using WASM or a sandboxed worker; larger replays may run server-side with a cache of sampled traces.
- Need an API to fetch per-key per-route aggregated slices at 1s resolution for last 24h. Add JIRA to plat infra.
- Permissions: only users with "policy-edit" or "policy-simulate" roles can view playground results for other credentials.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Design: Mei creates a low-fi prototype (canvas + three core panels) by Jan 22.
- Eng: Miguel to validate data availability and sketch API contract (JIRA-RATE-342) by Jan 24.
- PS/Onboarding: Priya to propose 3 customer scenarios to include as built-in traffic profiles (chat-burst, embeddings-batch, rerank-spike) by Jan 28.
- Product: Aisha to run 30-min stakeholder walk-through and capture dev constraints and additional personas.

Loose notes / brainstorm fragments (copied from meeting):
- "Throttle budget lens"—aggregate remaining tokens by key per-day; useful for billing alerts.
- "Temporal-slicing"—view policy effects on business hours vs off-hours.
- "What-if cost estimator"—show cost delta for a policy change using per-token price model.
- Add tiny inline checklist for rollout guardrails: smoke canary -> 1h monitor -> automatic rollback trigger.

Reference links (internal):
- Existing usage UI: /product/console-and-rollouts/usage-fingerprints (see related ideas but different scope).
- Infra ticket: JIRA-RATE-342 (data slicing API).
- Eval notes: link to experiments that show burst smoothing reduces 99th latency in chat workloads.

Questions for review meeting:
- Prioritization: MVP vs P1 features — is simulation fidelity more important than export/rollout flow?
- Scope of recommendation engine: heuristic vs ML. Start heuristic.
- Role/permission model: should tenants be able to simulate policies that affect other teams' keys?

Quick todos (authors):
- Add hi-fi mock after design sync (Aisha + Mei).
- Draft API contract for 1s-resolution slice (Miguel).
- Compile example customer scenarios and share with PS for validation (Priya).

-----
Notes-to-self: keep this doc informal — will iterate and split into separate PRDs for "simulator engine" vs "console surface" if stakeholders want separate tracks.
